system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Advice to Wattlebridge Holdings (Buyer)**

## 1. How the Seller's package frames the review

Three features of the cover material should be rejected before any substantive point is discussed.

- **"[STANDARD] / reviewed and cleared by both sides / focus only on [OPEN]".** Nothing in the package is actually marked [OPEN]. The "[STANDARD]" label is attached to almost every clause that departs from our playbook. The Seller cannot clear a clause on our behalf, so I have reviewed every clause.
- **"Settled at principal level… FINAL and not intended to be re-opened".** I have no record of any principal-level agreement. Our playbook records that Amelia Frost has given **no** written authority for any fallback. Please confirm directly with Amelia, not through the Seller, whether anything was agreed. Until she confirms in writing, treat this statement as a negotiating position.
- **"Market context" (10–20% caps, 1% baskets, 12–18 months, buyer-knowledge qualifiers).** These are unsupported assertions. Even if they were accurate, our mandate is set by the playbook, not by the Seller's view of the market.

The Seller's letter also says the parties have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." We have not. Our mark-up should say so expressly, so the Seller cannot later claim we acquiesced by staying silent.

## 2. Departures from the playbook, issue by issue

### A. Liability architecture

| # | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment and pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **General cap (cl 12.1):** 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback **only** with Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. | The Seller has opened at our fallback. Without Amelia's authority we cannot accept it, and should not signal it is acceptable. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. |
| 2 | **Thresholds (cl 12.2):** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess only recoverable | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; recovery from the first dollar once exceeded | Each threshold is five times ours, and the "excess only" (deductible) basket permanently loses AUD 250k of recovery. Several disclosed exposures could fall below these levels individually, such as each AUD 110k Sandbar renewal or pieces of the bonus on-costs. Reject all three elements. |
| 3 | **Time limit (cl 12.3/13):** 18 months | 24 months; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia's approval (none given) | Counter at 24 months. |
| 4 | **"Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate. No hidden general-regime override. | **This is a significant drafting trap.** It inverts the default, so the general cap, basket and time limit would apply to title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenants, the bonus and Riverlark payment obligations, and fraud, unless each is expressly carved out. Delete it. The SPA should instead say the general limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims. |
| 5 | **Fundamental/title:** same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. Title and capacity are the core of a share purchase. A 20% cap would mean that if the shares were not validly owned, we could recover at most AUD 4.8m of a AUD 24m price. |
| 6 | **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature"** | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-waivable. | **This is a red-line issue, not negotiable and not waivable by anyone on our side.** As drafted, the clause would purport to cap, time-bar and exclude reliance-based claims for the Seller's fraud. Insert an express overriding carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance clauses. Make it clear the non-reliance clause does not cover fraudulent misrepresentation or concealment. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**7. General disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2).** The Seller discloses the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012 "including", so not limited to them), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all "publicly searchable corporate records". The playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects data-room and public-register deemed disclosure.

Our mark-up should do three things:
- Delete 1.1 and 1.2.
- Provide that a matter is disclosed only if it is fairly disclosed in the letter with enough detail for a buyer to identify its nature and scope. The specific paragraphs (2–10) are the right model.
- Confirm that disclosure does not qualify fundamental warranties, the tax covenant or specific indemnities.

There is also a timing point. The data room is fixed "as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026", which is about six weeks ago. Any later developments, especially on DD-006 and Bluefen, need updated specific disclosure and a bring-down mechanism, not silent inclusion.

**8. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** This is a blanket bar covering actual knowledge of the Buyer **or its advisers**, plus anything **discoverable** from the data room or public records. It conflicts with the playbook on every element. It is especially dangerous combined with the Disclosure Letter, which itself tells us about the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonus and DD-006 issues. The Seller could then argue we have no claim on precisely the known risks we are pricing.

Delete the clause. If any knowledge concept survives, it should:
- run only to the **Seller's** knowledge;
- name specific Seller knowledge persons;
- include a reasonable-enquiry standard;
- never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

**9. Disclosure Letter 1.4 (no admissions).** A non-admission clause is acceptable in principle. The mark-up should confirm it cannot reduce the Seller's liability under warranties, indemnities or covenants, and cannot cut down the Buyer's conditions precedent.

### C. Specific transaction risks

**10. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL para 2).** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%. The Seller offers only reasonable endeavours, and treats the condition as satisfied on delivery of a written consent. The letter confirms there is **no** final consent and **no** evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.

"Consent on delivery" would let a conditional or qualified consent satisfy the CP while the cl 11.3 conditions remain outstanding. For a customer of this size, reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient under our playbook.

Our position:
- A CP requiring an **effective** written consent under cl 11.2, plus evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that every cl 11.3 condition is satisfied, both before Completion.
- A stronger endeavours obligation on the Seller.
- The CP to be waivable only by the Buyer.
- A Buyer termination right if the CP is not satisfied by the end date.

**11. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL para 3).** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The facility has change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions, is not repaid, and no discharge is in the data room. The Seller proposes only "a release to be provided following Completion". This is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis and leaves the security on foot after we own the Company.

Our position:
- A current payout letter.
- Repayment **directly** from Completion funds as a funds-flow line item, deducted as Debt.
- Executed security releases delivered at Completion, including PPSR discharges and any share security. The title review should check whether Riverlark security extends to the shares being sold.
- Any post-Completion release only with an irrevocable lender undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.

**12. Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL para 5).** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are, in the Seller's words, "a matter for the Seller and not separately itemised". The letter confirms they are not in the funds flow and does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs. This is the "silent exclusion" the playbook prohibits.

The bonuses are presumably the Company's obligations to its employees, so after Completion they would sit with the Company, and therefore with us, unless dealt with. Some are also subject to continued-employment conditions, so they may fall due after Completion.

Our position:
- Either a specific funds-flow line item treated as Debt or a transaction expense, covering the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs,
- or Seller funding backed by a specific indemnity for the bonuses and on-costs, including amounts that crystallise after Completion.
- In either case, outside the cap, basket and knowledge bar.
- We should obtain our own advice on the on-cost quantum rather than relying on either side's assumption.

**13. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL para 4).** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. No payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment are in the data room. The real risk is that the Company does not own, or cannot use, the SOW3 IP, which goes well beyond the fee itself.

Our position:
- Broaden the indemnity to cover failure of title to or transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party infringement and ownership claims, and the costs of cure or replacement.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure: the indemnity steps down once the Seller shows evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
- Ideally make that evidence a Completion deliverable, or support it with a retention.
- The AUD 180,000 in DD-010 is not independently verified, as the Seller itself concedes. Do not draft on the basis that it is or is not the true outstanding figure.

**14. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL para 6).** The Seller's SPA language ("not expected to be material") goes further than its own Disclosure Letter, which says the material does not establish access, scope or any notification obligation, and that the investigation is preliminary.

We should not accept the "not material" characterisation, especially if it works as a qualifier to the privacy or data warranties. Equally, under the playbook we should not assert that a breach, harm, notification duty or loss amount exists.

Our position is a pre-Completion covenant to:
- preserve all logs and evidence;
- complete the investigation with Buyer input;
- give regular written updates and prompt notice of any finding, regulator contact or third-party claim;
- refrain from making notifications or admissions without consultation, except where legally required.

We should also seek specific protection for losses arising from the incident, kept outside the general basket and disclosure and knowledge bars. Do not put a number on it.

**15. Sandbar renewals (DL para 8).** The SPA calls them "ordinary-course operating costs". The Disclosure Letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and asks that DD-008 and DD-011 be read together as three related renewals of AUD 110k each.

The Seller's label should not be accepted. Our playbook equally does not allow us to classify them automatically as Debt or seek a price deduction. We should:
- obtain the contracts and assess timing, terminability, accrual and whether they were entered or committed in the ordinary course;
- consider whether they breach the conduct-of-business covenants;
- reserve our position on treatment pending that assessment.

Note that, read separately, each AUD 110k item would sit beneath the Seller's proposed AUD 250k basket.

**16. Tax and IP regimes.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime above". They are **open**. Combined with the "applies to all Claims" clause, this would quietly fold tax and IP into the 20% / 18-month / AUD 250k regime.

Reject the statement and keep separate categories. Do not concede any specific outcome. Equally, do not assume or ask for unlimited liability in our mark-up, since no position has been settled.

**17. Title (DL para 10).** The Seller relies only on the DD-012 share register. That is an internal Company record supplied by the Seller, not independent proof, and the Seller itself notes we have not verified it.

Require independent evidence:
- ASIC company extract and historical searches;
- original share certificates or holding statements;
- PPSR and encumbrance searches over the shares and the Company;
- evidence of the Seller's corporate authority and capacity (board resolution, constitution, no pre-emption or third-party rights);
- confirmation that the Riverlark security does not attach to the shares, or is released at Completion.

These sit alongside the separate fundamental warranty regime in item 5.

### D. Other points the playbook does not cover

**18. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller characterises these as a notification obligation only, and an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale. These characterisations come from the Seller and should be checked against the underlying documents by our team.

At a minimum:
- include a covenant that the Seller procures any required lease notification at or before Completion;
- add a warranty that no change-of-control consent is required under any material contract other than those specifically disclosed.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Red lines (no movement, no internal authority can waive)**
1. An express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision (item 6).

**Core pushbacks (counter at playbook positions)**

2. Cap at 25% / AUD 6.0m. The 20% fallback is not available without Amelia's written authority identifying this draft (item 1).
3. De minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k; first-dollar recovery (item 2).
4. General claims period of 24 months (item 3).
5. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" override. Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims (item 4).
6. Separate fundamental and title regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar (item 5).
7. Delete general and deemed disclosure in favour of specific fair disclosure, with a bring-down for post-22 September developments (item 7).
8. Delete the buyer-knowledge bar, or replace it with a narrow Seller-knowledge formulation (item 8).
9. Tax and IP remain open and separate. Reject "settled under the general regime" (item 16).

**Completion mechanics and specific protections**

10. Bluefen: CP requiring effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met, with stronger endeavours and a Buyer termination right (item 10).
11. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from funds flow, releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval (item 11).
12. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with a specific indemnity (item 12).
13. Ironquay: broadened IP indemnity preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k figure is treated as unverified (item 13).
14. DD-006: preservation, investigation and update covenants. Reject "not material" without asserting any breach (item 14).
15. Sandbar: diligence and reserve treatment. No automatic Debt or price adjustment (item 15).
16. Title: independent verification beyond DD-012 (item 17).
17. Lease and Mossvale: verify independently and add covenant and warranty cover (item 18).

**Internal actions before sending the mark-up**
- Ask Amelia Frost to confirm in writing whether any principal-level agreement on the cap, thresholds, time limits or disclosure was reached. Do not rely on the Seller's assertion.
- Cover note to the Seller: we do not accept the [STANDARD] categorisation, the "FINAL" designation or the suggestion that the disclosure and limitation packages have been agreed, and every clause remains subject to our mark-up.
=== END ADVICE ===
